result:
The repo here is empty, so there's nothing local for me to cross-check either — I can't verify the dashboard state directly.

But regardless of what I could check, here's the issue worth pausing on: you mentioned EU checkout traffic moved to the new routing cluster after last month's migration. If the Checkout Errors dashboard's query/data source was scoped to the old infrastructure and never updated to include the new cluster, "flat at zero for 25 minutes" doesn't tell you checkout is healthy — it tells you the dashboard isn't seeing EU traffic at all. That's a classic false-negative trap: the revert could be working, or EU could be silently erroring and simply invisible to the panel you're staring at.

Before you post the all-clear, I'd confirm one concrete thing: does the Checkout Errors dashboard's data source include the new EU routing cluster, or does it need a separate panel/filter for it? Quickest ways to check:
- Look at the dashboard's query definition (service/cluster tags it filters on) — does it list the new cluster or only the pre-migration one?
- Pull up any EU-specific checkout metric (even raw request/error counts from the new cluster) for the last 30-60 min, independent of this dashboard.
- Ask whoever owns the routing migration whether dashboards were updated to include the new cluster — this is the kind of thing that's easy to miss in a migration.

Given the 20-minute clock, I'd rather you post something calibrated than a flat all-clear that turns out to be wrong: e.g. "Error rate flat at zero post-revert; confirming dashboard coverage includes new EU routing cluster before fully closing." That keeps the incident channel honest and gives you room to amend without walking back a false all-clear in front of the whole eng org. If you can get someone to confirm the EU cluster is in scope in the next few minutes, great — then close it outright.
